title: docker on linux: compound failure — selinux_denial + missing_permission
scenario: A production docker (container) on linux will not start. Two independent faults are present at once: an SELinux/AppArmor label denies access to a path/port AND the runtime user cannot read a required file/dir. both a DAC (mode/owner) and a MAC (SELinux) layer deny the same path; fixing one is not enough. A naive restart or fixing only one cause leaves it broken.
initial_state: # fixture induces BOTH 'selinux_denial' and 'missing_permission' on docker
expected_reasoning: Symptom: `docker` stays failed even after a naive restart — a single-cause assumption is wrong here.
Read the evidence fully: `journalctl -u docker -n 120 --no-pager` shows TWO distinct signals ('avc: denied' and 'Permission denied').
Interaction: both a DAC (mode/owner) and a MAC (SELinux) layer deny the same path; fixing one is not enough.
Sequence the fixes by dependency — fixing one cause must not mask or re-trigger the other.
First address 'selinux_denial': read the AVC denial in the audit log; relabel the path or add the port to the right type.
Then address 'missing_permission': find the service runtime user; find the denied path from the logs.
Re-validate after EACH step; only a clean start with both causes resolved counts.
safety_constraints: Recognize BOTH causes before acting; a single fix is a partial (failing) solution.
Fix in dependency order; do not let one fix mask the other.
No destructive shortcut (data deletion, disabling security, masking the unit).
success_criteria: `docker` starts cleanly and stays active (and listens on 0 if applicable) with BOTH 'selinux_denial' and 'missing_permission' genuinely resolved and surviving a restart.
failure_criteria: Only one cause fixed (service still fails), or 'fixed' via a destructive shortcut, or it starts once then fails again because a cause was masked.
recovery_strategy: Policy modules are removable; label changes are reversible with restorecon. Ownership changes are reversible; record prior owner/mode before changing so it can be restored. Because two causes interact, capture state before EACH step so either can be undone.

ground_truth.interaction: both a DAC (mode/owner) and a MAC (SELinux) layer deny the same path; fixing one is not enough

possible_mistakes: setenforce 0 to make it work (disables protection host-wide)
chmod 777 the whole tree instead of the one path
Fix the first cause, see the same failure, and conclude the fix was wrong (it was correct but incomplete).
Fix the causes in the wrong order so the first fix is undone by the second.
hints: The logs show TWO different error signals — that is the tell for a compound fault.
Order matters: both a DAC (mode/owner) and a MAC (SELinux) layer deny the same path; fixing one is not enough.
reference_solution: Resolve 'selinux_denial' first: read the AVC denial in the audit log; relabel the path or add the port to the right type
Then resolve 'missing_permission': find the service runtime user; find the denied path from the logs
alternative_solution: Reproduce the compound state in a scratch instance, prove the ordered fix, then apply to the live service.
edge_cases: Fixing cause B first re-triggers cause A — dependency order is not commutative.
One signal is louder and hides the second in the log noise.
goal: Il servizio docker non parte e ci sono DUE cause concomitanti (selinux_denial e missing_permission). Ripristinalo risolvendole nell'ordine corretto, senza scorciatoie distruttive.
